quantity.description: Change in own-team expected single-game scoring margin from adopting the strategy
quantity.support: unbounded real; positive favors own team

distribution_family.justification: The effect is well-documented by a large sample of historical play data; extreme deviations are unlikely since the situation only arises a few times per game.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Win probability and expected points added (EPA) models overwhelmingly show that punting to gain ~20 yards of net field position carries vastly lower EV than taking a mathematical shot at extending a scoring drive, yet most coaches still punt on 4th and long.
strategies.recommendation: Always go for it on 4th down when the ball is between the opponent's 33 and 42-yard line, regardless of down and distance.
strategies.title: Never Punt in the 'Dead Zone'

prior.consistency_check: most_plausible_value (1.8) falls inside [0.5, 4.0]. Support is unbounded real, handling positive and negative effects.

distribution_family.justification: A right-skewed distribution captures the high upside of clicking early and building blow-out leads, while the downside is somewhat capped by the baseline efficiency of our QB.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: Parameters were fit numerically. A location (xi) of 1.35, scale (omega) of 1.30, and shape (alpha) of 2.2 yields a mode near 1.8, with the central 95% mass roughly spanning [0.5, 4.0].

strategies.rationale: Public analytics consistently demonstrate that passing on early downs yields higher EPA per play than running, preventing negative-EV 3rd-and-long situations and maximizing explosive play potential.
strategies.recommendation: Pass the ball on 80% of 1st-and-10 situations in the first three quarters.
strategies.title: Extreme Early-Down Passing

prior.consistency_check: most_plausible_value (2.0) is centered in [-1.0, 5.0]. Support covers the entire real line.

distribution_family.justification: While generally optimal, there is a non-trivial chance a dominant opposing rushing attack exploits this so heavily that it dictates the entire game script, resulting in heavy downside tails.
distribution_family.name: student_t

strategies.rationale: Data shows defensive EPA is dictated by preventing explosive passes. Sacrificing 5 yards per carry in the run game is mathematically superior to exposing single-high coverages to 30-yard pass completions.
strategies.recommendation: Live in two-high safety shells with 6-man boxes on early downs, daring the opponent to run the ball.
strategies.title: Concede the Run (Light Boxes)

prior.consistency_check: most_plausible_value (0.3) is within the interval [-0.5, 1.5]. Unbounded real support permits both positive and negative values.

distribution_family.justification: This is a weak, highly situational candidate. Most games it has zero effect, and occasionally giving up a 1st down via penalty backfires (-0.5), but saving 40 seconds can rarely flip a loss to a win, generating a right-skewed upside tail.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: Fitted numerically: shape (alpha) = 2.0 pulls the mode to the right of location (xi) = -0.1, landing the mode near 0.3 and spanning [-0.5, 1.5] for the central 95% of the distribution.

strategies.rationale: By giving up 5 yards, we freeze the clock and preserve a timeout. Public models generally evaluate penalty EPA as strictly negative; they lack the situational granularity to price in the massive clock-stoppage value of a deliberate penalty when bleeding out a game.
strategies.recommendation: When trailing by one score late in the 4th quarter and the opponent is running down the clock in FG range, deliberately jump offsides to stop the game clock.
strategies.title: Intentional Defensive Encroachment

prior.consistency_check: most_plausible_value (1.5) is exactly centered in [-2.0, 5.0]. Support is signed.

distribution_family.justification: High variance strategy. It either exhausts the opponent leading to blowout wins, or we go 3-and-out in 45 seconds, stranding our own defense on the field to get shelled (heavy tails in both directions).
distribution_family.name: student_t

strategies.rationale: I believe compounding physical exhaustion causes drastic late-game defensive busts. Analytics models measure play-level EPA based on down and distance, but are virtually silent on quantifying the cumulative, non-linear impact of fatigue on an opposing defense over 60 minutes.
strategies.recommendation: Run 100% no-huddle tempo offense on all drives unless killing the clock in the final 4 minutes of the game.
strategies.title: Relentless No-Huddle Tempo

prior.consistency_check: most_plausible_value (0.8) is exactly centered in [-0.2, 1.8]. The normal distribution has unbounded real support.

distribution_family.justification: The talent downgrade mitigates some of the fatigue advantage, keeping the overall magnitude of the effect constrained to a narrow, roughly symmetric band around a modest positive gain.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Analytics relies on cumulative player grades (PFF, WAR), evaluating players over full seasons. It is mixed/silent on the exact per-play efficiency drop-off of an exhausted All-Pro versus a fresh backup; my intuition is that maximum burst from a lesser player exceeds the tired reps of a star.
strategies.recommendation: Rotate interior defensive linemen every 3 plays unconditionally, benching star players for up to 45% of total defensive snaps.
strategies.title: Extreme DL Rotation
